evidence: Cic. Agr. 2.75: tōtam Ītaliam suīs praesidiīs obsidēre atque occupāre (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: To seize, often before someone else can: a hill, a harbour, a seat. Its other senses: to fill or take up (time, space), to keep someone busy (see occupy-busy), to fall on someone, and to be first to do something: occupet extrēmum scabiēs, last one there’s a rotten egg (Hor. A.P. 417).

evidence: Caes. B.C. 1.44: legiō locum nōn tenuit (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Of keeping a place once taken: a position, a seat.
Properly to sit before a town, besiege or blockade it; then to beset and hold a place.

phrases.latin: occupat hic collem, cumbā sedet alter aduncā et dūcit rēmōs illīc, ubi nūper arābat
phrases.english: one takes to a hill, another sits in a curved boat and rows where lately he was ploughing

phrases.latin: dictū mīrābile, tenuit nōn sōlum āles captam semel sēdem
phrases.english: wonderful to tell, the bird not only kept the seat it had once taken
